question: The definitive treatment for coeliac disease in children is a strict lifelong gluten-free diet, which leads to reversal of villous atrophy and resolution of symptoms in most patients.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Coeliac disease treatment = lifelong gluten-free diet. Gluten elimination leads to restoration of villous architecture, antibody normalisation (anti-tTG IgA falls and should reach normal within 12–18 months), resolution of anaemia, and catch-up growth. Even trace gluten exposure perpetuates mucosal damage.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A strict gluten-free diet (avoiding wheat, barley, rye, and oats contaminated with gluten) is the only proven treatment for coeliac disease. Adherence leads to histological recovery (villous regeneration), normalisation of anti-tTG IgA antibodies, resolution of malabsorption, and catch-up growth. There is no role for immunosuppressive drugs in straightforward coeliac disease.
